title: A^2TG: Adaptive Anisotropic Textured Gaussians for Efficient 3D Scene Representation
claim: Selectively refine representation capacity in three stages: optimize, pick elements by gradient, then upscale each according to its geometry.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, bold arrows, panel (c) split into three dashed case boxes
description: A left-to-right pipeline of three rounded panels joined by thick black arrows, ending in a final output scene. Panel (a), Optimization, shows colored blurry 2D Gaussians (cyan streak, green ellipses, red and orange blobs) inside a dashed circle, with black arrows marking gradient directions. Panel (b), Gradient-Driven Gaussian Selection, overlays the same Gaussians on a grid of gray blocks whose shades show gradient magnitude. Panel (c), Adaptive Texture Upscaling, holds three dashed boxes with rules: if sx >> sy, T^u -> 2T^u; if sy >> sx, T^v -> 2T^v; if sx ≈ sy, both axes double. Small square-to-grid icons show the texture growing, next to before and after Gaussian pictures. The final scene on the right shows the upscaled textures. The eye goes first to the colorful Gaussians, then follows the arrows to the case boxes.
caption: Overview of gradient-based adaptive texture control. Given an initial 2DGS model, (a) our system first optimizes the parameters of the 2D Gaussians and their textures. (b) Next, we compute the positional gradient of the textured 2D Gaussians (as depicted in gray blocks) and select the 2D Gaussians that need to increase the resolution of the texture to capture more details. (c) Finally, we adaptively upscale the textures according to the anisotropy of the Gaussians.
abstract: Gaussian Splatting has emerged as a powerful representation for high-quality, real-time 3D scene rendering. While recent works extend Gaussians with learnable textures to enrich visual appearance, existing approaches allocate a fixed square texture per primitive, leading to inefficient memory usage and limited adaptability to scene variability. In this paper, we introduce adaptive anisotropic textured Gaussians (A$^2$TG), a novel representation that generalizes textured Gaussians by equipping each primitive with an anisotropic texture. Our method employs a gradient-guided adaptive rule to jointly determine texture resolution and aspect ratio, enabling non-uniform, detail-aware allocation that aligns with the anisotropic nature of Gaussian splats. This design significantly improves texture efficiency, reducing memory consumption while enhancing image quality. Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that A TG consistently outperforms fixed-texture Gaussian Splatting methods, achieving comparable rendering fidelity with substantially lower memory requirements. Project page: http://github.com/Rickyeeeeee/A2TG.
